A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RCS research and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Content can be matched despite substantial reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original detector evaluations on LLaVA, Qwen and InternVL, together with ablations, robustness analyses and SafeMTData adaptation experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains original detector evaluations and supplementary empirical analyses in the main text and appendices, with some numerical revisions.

M1.justification: The geometric layer-selection pipeline, last-token features, learned projection objectives, MCD/KCD scoring and thresholding are retained. Expanded explanations and redesigned diagrams do not establish a changed detection procedure.

E1.justification: The benchmark sources, benign distribution-shift scenarios, layer-selection datasets and SafeMTData task are retained. V1 Table 3 becomes v3 Table 6 with unchanged dataset coverage; streaming defense is discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: The motivational, main and appendix comparisons retain their comparator sets, including GradSafe, HiddenDetect, JailGuard, JailDAM, FLAVA classifiers and FDV. JailDAM (RCS) and JailDAM-RCS denote the same existing variant.

E3.justification: Dataset counts and splits, held-out attack families, evaluated model configurations, metrics and calibration procedures are retained. SafeMTData still uses 0–50 training examples and 100 test examples. No changed experimental protocol accompanies the revised result values.

E4.justification: The principal ablations and robustness plots are retained. However, v3 removes v1 Section 7's reported PCA preprocessing, smaller-MLP and regularization attempts to stabilize training. The condensed JailGuard analysis also omits the second FigTxt example and the robust-refusal FigStep case.

E5.justification: Main results retain 20 independent seeded runs with means, standard deviations and extrema. Adaptation and k-sensitivity experiments retain five runs. Revised F1 standard deviations change reported values, not uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: InternVL F1 values change between v1 Table 6 and v3 Table 5: GradSafe 74.9 to 62.9, HiddenDetect 81.2 to 54.6, and JailGuard 66.1 to 72.6; MCD/KCD F1 entries also change. Main LLaVA/Qwen results and quantitative plots are retained. V3 E.2 additionally reports score margins around 1–2.

T1.justification: Lemma 1, moved from D.2 to E.2, adds explicit benign-estimation accuracy assumptions and a guarantee stated uniformly across malicious clusters. Its proof sketch expands the benign/malicious error decomposition and locality reasoning while retaining the basic sample-complexity bound.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: RCS with MCD/KCD, safety-relevant internal representations, generalization to unseen attacks and lightweight pre-generation detection. Terminology and emphasis change without materially redefining these claims.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly acknowledges that streaming defense is unbenchmarked and qualifies the few-shot bound as explaining functional dependence rather than tight sample counts, with unmeasured constants. It also removes the 'near-perfect' characterization of 5–10-shot adaptation and elaborates JailGuard failure mechanisms.

D1.justification: V3 omits the explicit FLAVA last-layer extraction statement and the reported dropout range of 0.3–0.5 from stabilization trials. Most implementation information, including projection dimension, GPU hardware, baseline configurations and code-access information, is retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 and Appendix A substantially revise research positioning, adding reasoning hijacking, backdoors, fault injection, safety unlearning and comparisons with ACTOR and Adversarial Deja Vu. Representation-engineering coverage broadens, including concerns about superficial probing signals under distribution shift. These changes exceed bibliographic metadata updates.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting affects the introduction, method exposition, related work and limitations. Ablations receive numbered subsections, benchmark composition moves into a dedicated appendix, and lengthy JailGuard transcripts become structured case summaries.

P2.justification: V1's compact overview is replaced by separate layer-selection, projection and scoring diagrams, plus a new one-class-versus-contrastive illustration. The dataset table is enlarged and relocated, and multipage JailGuard example boxes become Table 15. Existing quantitative plots are retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer method illustrations, structured exposition and explicit qualifications of the few-shot theory and streaming applicability improve readability and transparency. The gain is limited by removed diagnostic detail and incomplete propagation of revised results: v3's InternVL layer-20 KCD F1 differs between Tables 5 and 11.
